1.status: Boundary holding. All routes remain closed. 412 households are within the order.
1.instructions: Residents are reminded to remain indoors after dark.
1.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

2.status: Boundary holding. No change to report. 411 households now stand registered.
2.instructions: Residents are reminded to remain indoors after dark.
2.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

3.status: Boundary holding. No change reported at any address in sectors 6, 9 and 11.
3.sighting: Distant activity logged at sector 6, beyond the even numbers of Morland Row.
3.instructions: Residents are reminded to remain indoors after dark.
3.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

4.status: The boundary is holding. No change recorded. Meters are to be read in all sectors.
4.instructions: Residents are reminded to remain indoors after dark. Thank you for your co-operation.
4.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

5.status: Boundary holding. No change reported. Two premises in sector 11 remain unoccupied.
5.sighting: Distant activity noted at sector 11, opposite the odd numbers.
5.instructions: Each household is reminded to keep its record of days complete and available.
5.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

6.sighting: Activity noted at sector 6, at the rear of the odd numbers.
6.instructions: Persons over sixty are reminded to keep to rear rooms between noon and four and indoors after dark.
6.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

7.status: Boundary holding. All routes remain closed. No change reported at 409 addresses.
7.sighting: Distant activity noted at sector 6, as on the third day, opposite the same three premises.
7.instructions: Households are reminded, on instruction, to remain indoors after dark and to be counted by day.
7.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

8.status: Boundary holding at sector 6. All returns from 409 households collected on time.
8.sighting: A movement near the sector 6 line has been accounted for. Residents need not repeat it further.
8.instructions: Residents of the even numbers are reminded to keep front glazing shuttered after dark.
8.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

9.status: Conditions across sectors 6, 9 and 11 are settled, orderly and entirely as expected.
9.sighting: The matter at the sector 6 line remains accounted for. Enquiries are no longer being taken.
9.instructions: Households in receipt of the allowance are reminded that it stands at four hours from the eleventh.
9.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

10.status: Boundary holding. Returns from sector 9 are delayed pending a further count.
10.sighting: Two movements at the sector 9 line shortly before first light are accounted for.
10.instructions: Every household is asked to keep the records of its occupants orderly and available.
10.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

11.status: Boundary holding. Conditions in the afternoon hours are unchanged at sectors 9 and 11.
11.sighting: The signal was sounded across sectors 6, 9 and 11 at ten past six. The apparatus is in order.
11.instructions: Persons awaiting examination are instructed to keep to the north rooms during the settled hours.
11.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

12.status: Boundary holding. Ration hours for households in sectors 9 and 11 stand as revised on the ninth.
12.sighting: Residents' accounts of the sector 6 movement now agree in every particular. The matter is closed.
12.instructions: Every household is reminded that the revised hours were circulated on the ninth.
12.closing: This has been the message from the Board.

13.status: All movement at the sector 9 line has been accounted for since the seventh.
13.sighting: One further movement at the sector 9 line remains unaccounted for and is under review.
13.instructions: Residents are reminded that nothing at sector 9 is outstanding and no report is required.
13.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

14.status: The order continues into a third week. Boundary conditions are not as they were on the first day.
14.sighting: Reports from sectors 6, 9 and 11 do not agree. Eleven households have made no return.
14.instructions: Every household is required to remain within its own rooms until further notice.
14.closing: This has been a message from the Board. It will not be repeated.

15.status: Boundary holding. Movement between addresses is closed from first light.
15.sighting: One lamp out at Morland Row. The man who saw to it is no longer on the register.
15.instructions: Residents are reminded to remain at their registered address and to open the door to no one.
15.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

16.status: The evening count was returned in full. The register is corrected to agree with it.
16.sighting: Lights were reported in every window of number 14. Its occupier is not listed.
16.instructions: Residents are reminded to report corrections to their own count before the evening broadcast.
16.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

17.status: Mrs Ayling of number 9 is appointed warden and will carry the register weekly.
17.sighting: A parcel was delivered to number 3. It was correctly addressed and no one posted it.
17.instructions: Residents are reminded to give Mrs Ayling their record when she calls and to keep nothing back.
17.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

18.sighting: The street was full at five o'clock and empty at six. The Board has no further detail.
18.instructions: The occupier of this address is reminded to remain within it.
18.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

19.status: Boundary holding. No change reported since the first day.
19.instructions: Residents are reminded to remain indoors after dark.
19.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

20.closing: This has been a message from the Board.

21.instructions: Residents are thanked for their cooperation. Mrs Ayling is thanked by name.

1.full.1: Morning. Mrs Ayling, number 9. I'll not keep you — I'm only going along the row.
1.full.2: That drain at the corner's blocked again. Third time since Easter and nobody's come.
1.full.3: Residents are reminded to remain indoors after dark. That's what they said. After dark.
1.full.4: I go up to the corner shop Tuesdays. If there's anything you want, you've only to say.
1.off.1: Morning. Mrs Ayling, I'll not keep you — I'm only going along past a few doors.
1.off.2: Residents are to remain indoors after dark. That's the words, or close enough to them.

9.full.1: I've the wireless on at nine sharp now. You get the whole of it if you're sat down first.
9.full.2: Settled, orderly and entirely as expected. Those were the words. I thought that was well put.
9.full.3: There's a right way to do a thing and it costs you nothing. I like knowing where I stand.
9.compressed.1: Residents are reminded to remain indoors after dark. That's what they said. After dark.
9.compressed.2: Card's by the door where they ask for it. No bother at all, once you're in the way of it.
9.off.1: I've the wireless on of a morning now. You get most of it if you're sat down in time.
9.off.2: Settled and orderly, they said. Entirely as expected — that's on the record, isn't it.

13.full.1: Nothing at sector 9 is outstanding. That's the instruction, and that's the end of it.
13.full.2: They said the one thing and then they said this. This is the one they've left standing.
13.full.3: I'll not argue with a correction. If it wanted arguing with they'd not have corrected it.
13.compressed.1: I go up to the corner shop Tuesdays. If there's anything you want, you've only to say.
13.compressed.2: No report's expected. So there's no report.
13.off.1: Nothing at sector 9 is outstanding, so they said. Or was it sector seven — I'd have to check.
13.off.2: They said one thing, then corrected it on the card. I'll not argue with a correction.

17.compressed.1: They've given me a clipboard. I'm to have your record when I call. It wasn't my idea.
17.compressed.2: I've lived up this road nineteen years. Don't make me ask you twice. Please don't.

18.compressed.1: The Board has no further detail. That's what I'm to say. That's the whole of what I have.
18.compressed.2: I saw it same as you did, and I've written down that I've no further detail.

20.compressed.1: I've to collect again and I don't know what for. Mr Sowerby does his and goes home.
20.compressed.2: You'll all still live up this road after. I've to think about that and I shan't.

5.full.1: I'm sorry to knock. It's the lady who was here before you I want, and I've the right house.
5.full.2: She had me down for the Tuesday, half three. It'll be on her calendar by the back door.
5.full.3: It's only two pound and a dish. My mother's dish. I'd not knock twice for less than that.
5.full.4: Say Mrs Hallow called. Her little one used to open this door to me herself.
5.off.1: I'm sorry to knock. It's the lady who had this house I'm after — I've the house, I think.
5.off.2: She had me down for half three sharp, the Tuesday just gone. I'd stake the hour on it.

10.full.1: Mrs Ayling at number 7 said to try you again. So here's me, and I'm sorry for it.
10.full.2: She had me down for the Thursday, half three. She's never once forgot a thing in her life.
10.full.3: It's only two pound and a dish. I'd not have troubled you, only the dish was my mother's.
10.compressed.1: I'm sorry to knock. It's the lady who was here before you I want, and I've the right house.
10.compressed.2: I'll try again Friday. I'd hate her to think I never called for it.
10.off.1: Mrs Ayling said to try again. Number 9, I think she said — or near enough to it.
10.off.2: She had me down for the Thursday, half three. It'll be on the calendar by the front door.

20.compressed.1: I'm sorry to knock again. It's the lady who was here before you, and I've the right house.
20.compressed.2: Two pound and the dish. Say Mrs Hallow called — she'll know the rest.

11.full.1: Miss Wren, Board enumerator. I'm to check the household record against what you say.
11.full.2: Household of one, is it? That's what's on file. I'll confirm it and move on.
11.full.3: Two names crossed off this row already this week. Yours isn't one of them.
11.compressed.1: Household of one, on file. I'll confirm it and move on.
11.off.1: Wren, Board enumerator — I'm to check the record against what you say, near enough.
11.off.2: Household of one, I make it. Or I did last time I wrote it down.

14.full.1: Back again. I'm to confirm the household record hasn't changed since the eleventh.
14.full.2: You'd be surprised how many change their answer between visits. Not accusing you.
14.full.3: I've got Mrs Ayling's name against yours for a witness, if it's ever wanted.
14.compressed.1: Confirming the household record hasn't changed. Same as the eleventh.
14.off.1: Back again. Confirming the household record, or near enough what I confirmed before.
14.off.2: I've a neighbour's name against yours for a witness. I'd have to check whose it was.

3.full.1: I'm Sylvia. Number 3. I can see your shoes. Have you got a pencil you don't want any more?
3.full.2: The one in the suit isn't a man. He's a big boy. You can tell from his neck and his wrists.
3.full.3: Here's the game. I say a word and you say the one after it. You can start.
3.full.4: Are you on your own in there? Nobody's come out of your door. I'm at the window a lot.

8.full.1: Mrs Pethick at number 12 says there's been a movement at the boundary. She said it twice.
8.full.2: It's been counted for. That's the words. Counted for, and nobody has to do a thing.
8.full.3: Did you see it? Everyone says it's counted for and nobody says what it was that moved.
8.full.4: The postman came twice yesterday. I've not seen him do that before.
8.compressed.1: Are you on your own in there? Nobody's come out of your door. I'm at the window a lot.
8.compressed.2: A movement at the boundary. I've got it right, haven't I. Say if I've got it wrong.

14.full.1: The  comes round the front of our house at ten and the back at four. I timed it.
14.full.2: Everyone keeps saying it's nearly done. It isn't nearly done. There's a whole week yet.
14.compressed.1: I'm Sylvia. Number 3. I can see your shoes. Have you got a pencil you don't want any more?
14.compressed.2: I'm still here. Nobody's said I have to stop coming to the door, so I've kept coming.

19.compressed.1: I've still got the pencil. I've not used it up. I'm keeping it for something good.
19.compressed.2: Mum says I'm not to stop long. I'm stopping a while. It's not raining much.

8.full.1: Board records. I check the card against our master copy — nothing further today.
8.full.2: There's a mismatch on the fourth. I note it, I don't resolve it. Not my role, that.
8.full.3: Your card says the sixth. Ours says the fifth. I'll write down both, if that's fine.
8.full.4: I'm not here to say who's right. I'm here so it's on file. That's the whole visit.
8.off.1: Board records. I check the card against a master copy — one of the copies, that is.
8.off.2: There's a mismatch on the fourth, or noted for the fifth now. I'd have to check my note.

10.full.1: My note from the eighth says the fifth. I'll go by my own note, if it's the same to you.
10.full.2: I copied that figure myself, off your card. I trust my hand over the card, honestly.
10.full.3: The master copy reads what I wrote down that day now, not what was on your card.
10.compressed.1: There's a mismatch on the fourth. I note it, I don't resolve it. Not my role, that.
10.compressed.2: Two boxes today. The figure, then my note on it. Then I'm gone.
10.off.1: My note from the eighth says the fifth, or it did the last I looked at my own note.
10.off.2: I copied that figure myself and I've checked it twice since. Trust the copy over the card.

13.full.1: I've the corrected figure with me. I'm comfortable with it, same as the broadcast.
13.full.2: If your card disagrees with the correction, I'll note the disagreement and leave it.
13.full.3: The correction's the correction. I don't need your book to agree with it today.
13.compressed.1: Your card says the sixth. Ours says the fifth. I'll write down both, if that's fine.
13.compressed.2: Figure, then the note. Then I'm away.
13.off.1: I've the corrected figure with me. Comfortable with it, same as the broadcast, near enough.
13.off.2: If your record disagrees, I'll note it. I'll not say which one of us has it right.

6.full.1: Dr Marchant, Board medical. A short list of questions and a sheet to put the answers on.
6.full.2: Sleeping — through, or in pieces? And what time you woke, as near as you can put it.
6.full.3: Appetite, and headaches or none. I write down what you say. I don't write what I think of it.
6.full.4: Now say the last three days back to me, in order. Most people can't. It isn't a test.

11.full.1: Sleeping. You told me five last time; I've six here in my own hand. One of us slipped.
11.full.2: Headaches — you said none. I'll ask it again and put today's answer down as today's.
11.full.3: Mr Sowerby carries the compliance card. I've the health sheet. Different papers entirely.
11.compressed.1: Now say the last three days back to me, in order. Most people can't. It isn't a test.
11.compressed.2: Sleep, appetite, head. Three words each and I'll not keep you standing.

15.compressed.1: I needn't trouble you today. Where there's no new answer the sheet takes last week's.
15.compressed.2: Nothing to ask. You're marked as before. Good afternoon to you.

4.full.1: Liddell, GPO. I'm to check the line — shouldn't take more than a few minutes.
4.full.2: No telephone in? That's on my sheet as installed. I'll note the discrepancy.
4.full.3: Happens more than you'd think. A sheet's only as good as the last man who wrote on it.
4.compressed.1: GPO. Line's not here to check. I'll note it and move on.
4.off.1: Liddell. GPO — I'm to check the line, or that's what the sheet has me down for.
4.off.2: No telephone? I'll have that as installed. Or nearly installed. I'd have to check twice.

10.full.1: Liddell again. Still nothing on my sheet to say the line's been struck off.
10.full.2: I'll keep coming till somebody higher up tells me to stop. That's the whole of my job.
10.full.3: Funny thing, doing a job that's never once been needed. I've made my peace with it.
10.compressed.1: Still nothing struck off my sheet. I'll keep coming till told otherwise.
10.off.1: Liddell again, or it might be my second call — I've lost which visit this is.
10.off.2: Nothing struck off my sheet. Or nothing I've checked struck off, I should say.

9.full.1: I'm Mrs Corrigan. I'm stopping near here for now, since my own street was cleared.
9.full.2: They cleared my road a fortnight back. I couldn't tell you why. They don't say why.
9.full.3: I'm not in my own house. Billeted, is the word they use. It's somebody's spare room.
9.full.4: My street's still standing, far as I know. I've just not been let back to it since.

12.full.1: I did say to someone the hours might change. I never thought they'd repeat it on.
12.full.2: I mentioned it in the queue, that's all. I never said I'd heard it off anyone official.
12.full.3: Everyone's saying it now. I only said what I thought might happen, the once.
12.compressed.1: I'm not in my own house. Billeted, is the word they use. It's somebody's spare room.
12.compressed.2: Funny, hearing your own thought said back at you by someone else entirely.

14.compressed.1: I'm Mrs Corrigan. I'm stopping near here for now, since my own street was cleared.
14.compressed.2: I've kept my case half packed since I got here. Habit, I expect. You do get in the way of it.

4.full.1: Gas board. I'll do the meter and be out your road. Don't get up, I know where it is.
4.full.2: I've been under more sinks on this row than the man that put them in. Mind the flap.
4.full.3: The one before you never lit the back room. A reading like that for a year, near enough.
4.full.4: Two mantles of an evening and you'll feel it by Friday. Most light the one and stop by it.
4.off.1: Gas board. I'll have done the meter Tuesdays, near enough, since I started this walk.
4.off.2: The one before you kept to the back room a good while. A neighbour told me that, I think.

9.full.1: It's come down. Not my doing — I've said so at every door today and I'll say it here.
9.full.2: Four hours a day from the eleventh. Four. That's on the notice, not just me saying it.
9.full.3: I don't mark your card, that's the warden's. I only put the figure in my own book.
9.off.1: It's come down, so I'm told. I've said as much at every door, or near enough all of them.
9.off.2: Four hours a day, or thereabouts, from the eleventh. I'll not swear to the exact count.
9.compressed.1: Gas board. I'll do the meter and be out your road. Don't get up, I know where it is.
9.compressed.2: Four hours, from the eleventh. I'd put that down somewhere if I were you.

16.compressed.1: Still on the round. Eleven years I've done this street and I've done it today.
16.compressed.2: Reading's the same as last week. I'll put it down as I found it.

3.full.1: ...no cause for alarm at any address on...
3.full.2: You are safer inside than you are out here.
3.full.3: ...door to door, in order, and then we're...
3.full.4: It is nothing to worry about and nothing to sign.
3.full.5: ...tell you my name, only they'd rather I...

6.full.1: There is no cause for alarm at any address on this street.
6.full.2: You are safer inside than you are out here.
6.full.3: It is nothing to worry about and nothing to sign.
6.full.4: We're going door to door, in order, and then we're away by five.
6.full.5: I'd tell you my name, only they'd rather I didn't. It isn't a secret, it's the form.

11.full.1: The  has not moved all week. Nobody has said different to me.
11.full.2: The shutters are as they were. That part I can answer for you.
11.full.3: I'm not being funny with you. I've told you what I'm able to tell you.
11.compressed.1: There is no cause for alarm at any address on this street.
11.compressed.2: The  is where it was. I've nothing else for you.

18.compressed.1: I came back round, like I said I would.
18.compressed.2: There is no cause for alarm at any address on this street.

1.full.1: Morning. Two on the step, same as always. I'll leave three if you're wanting it.
1.full.2: Been doing this row since before the war ended. You get to know a door by its milk.
1.full.3: Empties out by eight or I can't promise they'll get taken. Creatures of habit, us.

3.full.1: Two again. I'll not ask questions, I just count what's out and leave what's asked.
3.full.2: Quiet round this week. Fewer bottles out on this row than I'd expect for the season.
3.full.3: I'll be past again Thursday. Same time, same count, unless you tell me otherwise.
3.compressed.1: Two on the step, same as always.

7.full.1: Two again, and I'll say it plain: fewer of you taking milk than a fortnight back.
7.full.2: Mrs Pethick took hers in early today. Usually waits till I've gone past next door.
7.full.3: I'll keep coming while there's a round to keep. Can't promise past that, mind.
7.compressed.1: Two on the step. Fewer taking it than there were.

1.full.1: I said to Ron, she'll have run out of tea by Thursday, and here I am with a quarter of it.
1.full.2: You had the front door painted the summer before last. Green, wasn't it. Lovely job.
1.full.3: Your mother stood on that step and told me she couldn't abide the draught off this street.
1.full.4: Three windows at the front and you only ever open the two. I'd be the same.
1.full.5: Anything you want fetching, you knock on the wall. Two knocks. I'll hear it.
1.off.1: I'll have been past this morning, though I couldn't tell you the hour of it.
1.off.2: Two of you knocked here today, or was it the door that did — I've lost which.

4.full.1: Two windows at the front. I said three the other day and I was wrong. Two.
4.full.2: The door was green. The summer before last. Green, and they came on the Tuesday.
4.full.3: I slept, I had my breakfast, I came round. All of it in the right order.
4.full.4: Your mother on that step, about the draught. I've thought about it every day since.
4.full.5: You knock twice on the wall. Two knocks. That's ours, that is.
4.off.1: I'll have been past on the Tuesday, or near enough it — the days run on a bit now.
4.off.2: You knocked on the wall, same as always. I heard it plain enough, the once.

7.full.1: They're asking everyone on this street the same question and I'd rather it came from me.
7.full.2: I've told them what I remember. I'd like it to match what you remember.
7.full.3: You'll say the door was green, won't you. The summer before last. Green.
7.full.4: Nobody is in trouble. It's a list, and a list wants the same answer twice.
7.full.5: If you'd rather I stopped asking, I'll stop. We'll stand here and not say anything.
7.off.1: I've filled in my own form already. I'd like yours to match it, if it's no trouble.
7.off.2: Nobody's in any trouble, I don't think. I've said that at every door today.

8.full.1: A sighting near the boundary. Near. That's the word they used, near.
8.full.2: Reported near it, not at it. Ron says that's a different thing and I think he's right.
8.full.3: I've said it back to myself twice so I'd have it right for you.
8.full.4: They're careful with their words and I've decided that's a kindness.
8.full.5: Two at the front. I keep saying it to myself. Two.
8.compressed.1: A sighting near the boundary. Near.
8.compressed.2: Anything you want fetching, you knock on the wall. Two knocks. I'll hear it.
8.off.1: A movement near the boundary. That's the word going round, near enough.
8.off.2: I've said it back to myself so I'd have it right. Near enough is right enough.

12.full.1: It was a rumour on the Tuesday and a fact by the Thursday and now nobody heard it clearly.
12.full.2: I'm not saying I heard it. I'm saying I know it. That's a different thing, isn't it.
12.full.3: You had the flu the week Dad died. You didn't come to the house. That's just what happened.
12.compressed.1: Two at the front. Two. I've always said two.
12.compressed.2: You had the front door painted the summer before last. Green, wasn't it. Lovely job.
12.off.1: It was a rumour on the Tuesday, or might have been the Wednesday — I've lost the day.
12.off.2: I'm not saying I heard it. I'm saying I've confirmed it. That's different, isn't it.

16.compressed.1: You saw it as well, then.

2.full.1: Nurse Fairhurst. I do the rounds while the surgeries are shut — won't keep you long.
2.full.2: Dr Marchant sends his rounds through me now, while he's stretched thin himself.
2.full.3: Nothing to note for your address. I'll mark the form and be on my way.
2.compressed.1: Rounds, while the surgeries are shut. Nothing to note for you.
2.off.1: Nurse... Fairhurst. Rounds, while the surgeries are shut — I'll not keep you a moment.
2.off.2: Dr Marchant has me doing his rounds now. Or near enough his rounds, this week.

7.full.1: Back again. Nothing's changed at your address since the second, I'll note that down.
7.full.2: You're eating, sleeping? I only ask because I'm meant to ask. Say what you like.
7.full.3: Fewer houses on my list than I had. The surgeries reopen soon enough, they say.
7.compressed.1: Nothing's changed at your address. I'll note it and be on.
7.off.1: Back again, or near enough the second time. I've lost count of the rounds, honestly.
7.off.2: Nothing's changed at your address, so I've written. I'd stand by that, more or less.

2.full.1: Ken. Ken Dalgleish. I've had this walk since before they put the new boxes in.
2.full.2: There's still post coming for the one before you. I bring it till somebody tells me not to.
2.full.3: Nine takes two papers and ten takes none. I know this street by what goes through the door.
2.full.4: Mrs Pethick's had a card off her sister every week since the summer. Never misses.
2.off.1: Ken. I've had this walk a good while now — I couldn't tell you exactly how long.
2.off.2: There's still post for the one before you. It's on my record to keep bringing it.

7.full.1: It's all come at once today. They'd been holding the lot at the office and now they've not.
7.full.2: One delivery a day from here on, and it'll be the morning. That's the order, it's not mine.
7.full.3: Nothing for half the row and four for you. That's how it falls when it's been stacked up.
7.full.4: Two more for the one before you. I'd open them, myself. It's your door they came to.
7.off.1: It's all come at once today, or near enough all of it. They'd had it a good while.
7.off.2: One a day from here on. Or that's the order — I've had it returned to me twice already.

12.full.1: They had it at number three: the ration hours changed on the eighth. Everybody's heard it.
12.full.2: I've it off Mrs Ayling at nine, who had it off the warden. So it's not a rumour, is it.
12.compressed.1: There's still post coming for the one before you. I bring it till somebody tells me not to.
12.compressed.2: It changed on the eighth. Ask anyone on the row and they'll tell you the same.
12.off.1: They had it at number three: the allowance changed on the eighth. Everybody's heard it.
12.off.2: I've had it off two others now, so it's not just the one telling me the same thing.

17.compressed.1: Parcel on the round. Right name on it, right number, and no postmark anywhere on it.
17.compressed.2: It wants signing for. I'll get it signed and that's me away till tomorrow.

6.full.1: Rag and bone! Bottles, iron, old clothes — I'll take whatever you don't want.
6.full.2: That kitchen chair, the one with the leg glued — you weren't about to keep it?
6.full.3: Thirty years on this row. You get a nose for what a house is about to lose.
6.full.4: No charge for looking today. I'll come back Tuesday, if you've changed your mind.

13.full.1: Rag and bone, same as ever. The wireless doesn't tell me what to weigh.
13.full.2: Corrected or not, iron's iron. I'll take it the same either way, love.
13.full.3: Everybody's fretting over that broadcast. Can't say it's troubled me at all.
13.full.4: Board's clipboard has been up and down this row twice today. Keeps them busy, I suppose.
13.compressed.1: Rag and bone! Bottles, iron, old clothes — I'll take whatever you don't want.
13.compressed.2: Same cart, same round. Nothing's outstanding on my sheet, whatever's on theirs.

20.compressed.1: Same as ever on this row. I'll be back Thursday, same as I always have been.
20.compressed.2: Rag and bone, still. Nothing's changed for me — I'll take what's going spare.

2.full.1: Mum's kettle is still in the cupboard over the sink. The one with the handle burnt through.
2.full.2: You've had that chair by the window since you moved in. You always did face the street.
2.full.3: You broke your wrist off the shed roof on a Tuesday. The ninth. Quarter past four, it was.
2.full.4: I've put the pears on the step. Don't come out till I'm at the gate, they're funny.
2.full.5: You never write. I'm not having a go. I'd just like to know you're putting things down.

5.full.1: Gran's was Ardwick Terrace, number eleven. You used to say twelve and you were wrong then.
5.full.2: Dad drove us to Rhyl that summer, not the coach. You slept the whole way, there and back.
5.full.3: There was a dog. Rusty, or Rusker. I've said Rusty for years and nobody's stopped me yet.
5.full.4: You've a mark on the back door where the pram went through. Go and look, it's still there.
5.full.5: I'd not tell anyone what you keep in that book. Not because of anything. It's just yours.

9.full.1: I want you to know — and I do mean this — that I've thought about you every day of it.
9.full.2: Say it back to me. Not for me. Say it so you've said it out loud in your own house.
9.full.3: You had the flu the week Dad died. You didn't come to the house. That's just what happened.
9.full.4: I'm not going to cry on your step. I'll do that in the car and you'll never have to see.
9.full.5: Ask me anything about us. Go on, I'd like you to. I'd like that to be on the record.
9.compressed.1: You never write. I'm not having a go. I'd just like to know you're putting things down.
9.compressed.2: I've thought about you every day of it.

10.full.1: I saw it myself. Thursday, about six. Three of them at the fence by the allotments.
10.full.2: It was still light, mind. Four at the outside. Two men, and one of them was carrying.
10.full.3: The fence I mean is the one behind the school, not the allotments. I've said that wrong.
10.full.4: Whatever it was, nobody hurried. That's the bit I keep coming back to. Nobody hurried.
10.compressed.1: I'd not tell anyone what you keep in that book. Not because of anything. It's just yours.
10.compressed.2: Put it down if you want. I'll say the same tomorrow.

14.full.1: I've had the whole walk here to think what to say and I've come with nothing. So. Here.
14.full.2: You were right about the coach to Rhyl. Dad never drove us. I've had that wrong for years.
14.full.3: Your gate's off its hinge. It was off in May as well. Nobody's coming to see to it now.
14.full.4: I stood in your hall a minute before I knocked. It smells like Gran's did. I don't know.
14.full.5: If I've any of it wrong, tell me and I'll put it down your way. I've brought a pencil.

19.compressed.1: You've a mark on the back door where the pram went through. Go and look, it's still there.
19.compressed.2: I've brought the pears. Don't come out till I'm at the gate.

6.full.1: You keep the milk on the inside sill, not the step. You always have. Cold enough, isn't it.
6.full.2: That back bedroom door sticks when it's wet. You lift it by the handle to get it shut.
6.full.3: You had a bad winter the year before last. Six weeks off work. Nobody made a fuss of it.
6.full.4: Your mother's name was Eileen. She'd have been eighty in March. I hope you marked it.
6.full.5: I'll not keep you. You'll need the wireless on at four. You never miss it, do you.

13.full.1: You've moved the chair. It used to face the window. I could see that from the gate.
13.full.2: You take the stairs on the left side. The right one gives. You've done that from the start.
13.full.3: Your writing slopes back when you're tired. It always did. I don't mind saying I liked it.
13.full.4: You had a bicycle with a basket on it. Green. You kept it in the passage and it rusted.
13.compressed.1: You keep the milk on the inside sill, not the step. You always have. Cold enough, isn't it.
13.compressed.2: I'll not keep you. It's nearly four.

17.compressed.1: I've brought something of your mother's back. You'll not remember lending it. That's fine.
17.compressed.2: You put it down wrong, but I'd not change it. It reads better the way you had it.

3.full.1: Prentice. I'm to tune the piano — same arrangement as always, this time of year.
3.full.2: No piano? That's queer. I've had the standing arrangement a fair while now.
3.full.3: I'll not charge for a wasted call. If it turns up, you know where to find me.
3.compressed.1: No piano? That's queer. Standing arrangement, this time of year.

12.full.1: Prentice again. I did wonder if I'd got the wrong house, but the name's the same.
12.full.2: Still no piano, I take it. I'll not keep asking, but I'll not forget it either.
12.full.3: That postman's been later on his round this week. Not that it's my place to remark.
12.compressed.1: Still no piano. I'll not forget the arrangement, whoever it's with.

4.full.1: I'm a Bell, from along the row. There's two of us — people mix us up, always have.
4.full.2: It's me you want, the one with the scar on this thumb. My sister's is the other hand.
4.full.3: Even Mrs Pethick gets us backwards, and she's known us the longest of anyone here.
4.full.4: We take it in turns calling. Saves the pair of us knocking on the one door at once.

11.full.1: My sister said you'd asked after the broadcast. She'd not have got that wrong.
11.full.2: She told me it's my scar on the left thumb. I could have sworn it was my right.
11.full.3: You'll have to forgive her if she's told you something twice. She does that lately.
11.compressed.1: We take it in turns calling. Saves the pair of us knocking on the one door at once.
11.compressed.2: She'll have said it better than I will. She always was the one for talking.

17.compressed.1: It's my thumb with the scar, not hers. Or it's hers. I've lost track which, myself.
17.compressed.2: Don't go by the thumb. We've never once been able to, and we're the ones who'd know.

5.full.1: I'm to confirm your last collection, with the date. Not what you recall — what you wrote.
5.full.2: And the day activity was first noted at sector 6. Your figure, please — not ours.
5.full.3: May I see the record? There's a box for it and I can't leave the box empty.
5.full.4: The card by your door has the fourth. If your book has the third, one of the two is a slip.
5.full.5: That was the eleventh, not the ninth. I'll put it right in the margin — saves you the asking.

8.full.1: There's a line on the sheet for the sector 6 movement. There's always been a line for it.
8.full.2: The announcement of the movement at the line — the day you heard it, from your own record.
8.full.3: Front glazing shuttered since the eighth. I'm to ask, not to inspect. Say yes, or say when.
8.full.4: New card, same door. The old one is collected. That is the procedure, as ever.
8.full.5: If you noted anything at the line yourself, there's a box. Day and number, nothing further.
8.compressed.1: May I see the record? There's a box for it and I can't leave the box empty.
8.compressed.2: Two boxes today. The movement, then the shutters. Then I'm away.

13.full.1: The correction stands. Nothing at sector 9 is outstanding. That is the sheet I'm working to.
13.full.2: If your book has the movement unaccounted for, your book has the earlier reading. I'll mark it.
13.full.3: Day, then number. That is all today's sheet wants of you.
13.compressed.1: I'm to confirm your last collection, with the date. Not what you recall — what you wrote.
13.compressed.2: Number. Then the day. Then I'm away.

15.compressed.1: Only the card today. You needn't fetch the book down.
15.compressed.2: Nothing to confirm. It's filled in already.

20.compressed.1: Twentieth. Everything's marked but tomorrow's initial, and I've the pen for that.
20.compressed.2: Nine tomorrow, then the file goes in. Same as every house on the row.

15.full.1: Cole. Street watch now. In or out's all today's sheet wants — not the book.
15.full.2: One line covers you: door shut or not. That's what I'm recording, nothing further.

18.compressed.1: One line covers you: door shut or not. That's what I'm recording, nothing further.
18.compressed.2: Today's logged as normal. I didn't see it happen, so I don't write that I did.

21.compressed.1: Sheet's signed. Quiet street, nothing outstanding — I'm through for the night.
21.compressed.2: Whatever's through that door come morning isn't mine to log. I'm off home.

16.full.1: They've corrected the count. I said it wouldn't want saying twice, and it didn't.
16.full.2: I still lay his plate of an evening. It costs nothing, saying it out or not.

19.compressed.1: They've corrected the count. I said it wouldn't want saying twice, and it didn't.
19.compressed.2: I know I've said that before. I couldn't tell you when.

20.compressed.1: Nothing left to do today. I sat with him a while, same as always.
20.compressed.2: You'll all still be here tomorrow, I shouldn't wonder. I'll not be long.

residue-shopping-list: Bread. Milk. The good tea, not the everyday.
Two chops, if the butcher has any left by Friday.

A spare bulb still in its wrapper on the landing shelf.

1: traffic on the main road, voices past the window, a bus grinding gears, a radio next door
2: the same traffic, someone laughing at the corner, the late bus, a radio turned up loud
3: cars along the row, voices by the gate, the bus on its hour, a wireless two doors down
4: traffic down to occasional cars, one bus passing near-empty, a single voice, a faint radio
5: a car now and then, one voice down the street, and a dog barking two gardens over
6: barely a car all morning, someone's wireless faint through the wall, the dog again
7: an occasional car, a single voice at the gate, the dog carrying from behind the row
8: a car passing rarely, no radio today, the dog barking off toward the allotments
9: one voice, then nothing, the dog barking late and further off than usual
10: no engines at all today, a bird calling from the guttering
11: birds in the yard at first light, nothing else moving
12: birdsong along the row, no cars, no voices at all
13: birds again at dawn, the street otherwise still
14: birds calling through the morning, the house around them quiet
15: no birdsong today, only wind picking up in the eaves
16: wind in the eaves, a loose slate somewhere above
17: wind against the glass, nothing else audible
18: rain on the window, the eaves running, wind dropping toward dusk
19: no wind, no rain, only the house settling into itself
20: a quiet that isn't the street's, a board finding its own temperature
21: the house's own tone, nothing arriving from outside it at all

1: Someone has swept the step two doors down; nobody has swept yours.
2: The water tastes of iron today.
4: The post came at the wrong hour.
6: A window on the landing faces a blank wall; no building stands beyond it.
7: The number on next door's post has been written over in a different hand.
9: There is a smell of burning that is not in this room.
10: Two milk bottles wait on the step where you are sure you set out only one.
11: A sound comes through the party wall that isn't quite a voice.
12: The compliance card by the door carries a stamp from a date you don't recognise.
13: The stair by the turn creaks on a different step than it did last week.
14: A key that fits nothing sits heavier in your pocket than it did yesterday.
15: The light in the hall was on and you are certain you did not light it.
A cup you'd emptied sits in the sink with water in it.
16: A float passes the window at an hour the milkman never once kept.
17: Someone plays four notes on a piano, twice, from further down the row.
18: It rained when the broadcast said it wouldn't, or you remember sun instead.
A photograph on the stairs hangs crooked however often it's straightened.
20: The chalk mark on the doorframe has been drawn over in the same place twice.
21: The hall clock ran fast today by the same amount it ran slow yesterday.
The kettle was hot before the gas had been lit long enough to warm it.

1: You open the journal at the desk. The entry from this morning is there exactly—your
hand, the ink the same colour. You close the book and go to sleep.
2: You turn to yesterday's entry. The time is wrong. Not badly wrong—off by an hour, like
you misread your watch. The ink is the same age as the paper around it. You read it
twice and the time is still wrong.
3: The kitchen has become the hall. You read the entry back and that is what it says. But
you saw something yesterday that has no name in your vocabulary, and you cannot write
it. The page has a blank where a word should be, and no word exists to fill it.
4: An entry appears in your hand, dated from three days ago. The handwriting is yours.
You do not remember writing it. You were asleep that night, or you were somewhere
else—the day is blurred. Two other entries have drifted in the meantime.
5: One entry says the visitor came on Tuesday. The second entry, written on Tuesday, says
they did not come. You read them aloud to make sure you are reading correctly. Neither
6: The page numbers skip from 47 to 51. The space between is blank. And the entry you
locked with tape three nights ago—the one you wanted to keep—has drifted anyway. The
tape is still sealed around it.
7: You open the journal to a page dated six days in the future. It is written in your
hand. The ink is fresh. You will not write these words for almost a week, and they are
8: Three separate entries have shifted since yesterday. The journal feels heavier. You
hold it at arm's length and then set it down.
9: There is a full entry, in your hand, from a day you do not remember living. The words
cohere into a coherent account. Your handwriting. Your way of noting the time. You
have no memory of writing it.
10: Page 63 ends and page 65 begins. Pages 64 is gone. Page 71 is gone. The numbering
skips like missing teeth. You turn the pages and count to make sure you are seeing
11: One entry says it happened. Another entry, from that same day, says it did not. You
read them in sequence. You read them backwards. Both remain what they were written as.
The clock on the landing has stopped.
12: Pages that were present yesterday are gone. Pages that were not here yesterday are
present. The numbering breaks and restarts itself. One entry is written in your hand
and is dated two days ago, but you did not write it two days ago.
13: Multiple entries have shifted from where they were. Multiple entries now contradict
each other. You sit at the desk with the open journal. The day you just lived is on
the page in front of you. You do not recognize it.
14: You wake knowing something occurred. The night was solid and real. There are no words
for it. The vocabulary does not have them. You sit at the desk and the page stays
empty because you have nothing to write. The silence is yours alone.
15: The journal shifts in your hands when you open it. Several entries have drifted since
you last checked them. Some of them now contradict things you are certain of. You set
the book down without reading further.
16: An entry is there, dated today, entirely in your hand. You have no memory of writing
it. The words read as something you might have said, if you were speaking yourself to
17: Two entries now describe the same moment differently. You remember seeing this moment
replayed to you. The entry in your hand is what you remember. The replay was wrong.
You will never tell anyone what you remember, because no one else will believe there is
18: Pages vanish between one night and the next. Other pages shift. The numbering is
ruined. You spend an hour flipping backwards through the journal, trying to find a
19: Your own words are returned to you wrong. Some entries replay exactly as you wrote
them. Others are played back with details you know you never wrote. You lie in the bed
and watch. The page stays empty because you are watching, not writing.
20: Entries appear that do not belong to the structure of your days. Earlier entries now
contradict them in ways that cannot be resolved. The replays continue underneath. You
21: The final night shifts what remains. Multiple entries change. You turn the pages in the
morning light. By the time you reach the end, you are reading the record of someone
who lived here, in this house, in these days. You cannot be certain it was you.

compliance: The broadcast ends. The light moves through the window and is gone.
Nothing knocks at the door. You lock it. Upstairs, the landing is empty.
The bedroom door is closed. The bed is there. You lie down. You sleep.
rupture: You open the kitchen door. The kitchen is there. You reach to turn on the light.
Your hand finds the wall in the wrong place. You pull back. The oven is also wrong.
You step toward it. The space does not hold. You step back. The room is still there and still wrong.
synchronisation: You read the entries in order. The true ones are there: eleven windows counted and verified.
Three landings. The mark on the doorframe. The handwriting on the tins is yours and legible.
These fit. The false ones do not fit—a word in the wrong place, a detail that dissolves.
They are passed over. What was distributed across twenty-one days is now gathered.
Nobody will know if you were right. The page ends. The house is quiet.

eileen-case-note: A folded note in Eileen's sewing case reads:

options.label: Take the pears in before they bruise.
options.reply: All right. I heard you move. Keep the soft one for yourself.

options.label: Leave them on the step, where she put them.
options.reply: That's fine. The birds will have them by morning, then. They always do.

options.label: Answer her without opening the door.
options.reply: You sound like Dad when you do that. Not the words. The place you put them.

options.label: Slide the pencil through the letterbox.
options.reply: Thank you. Don't shut it yet. I want to hear the house think.

options.label: Keep the pencil. Tell her you have none to spare.
options.reply: That's all right. I can use the red one. It writes when it wants to.

options.label: Ask why she needs it before you answer.
options.reply: For the numbers. They keep changing when I look away.

options.label: Show him the whole journal, open flat.
options.reply: Thank you. That is more than the box requires. I won't read the private parts.

options.label: Show him only the page with the collection card.
options.reply: That will do. You have kept the useful distinction. Most people don't.

options.label: Close the book and say the record is personal.
options.reply: Of course. Personal is a category. I'll write “not produced” and come again.

options.label: Let Denise's version stand.
options.reply: Thank you. I wanted you to say that, but not because I wanted to win.

options.label: Ask whether the rest of her memory is wrong too.
options.reply: There it is. I give you one thing back and you weigh the whole house with it.

options.label: Offer her the pencil and ask what she wants remembered.
options.reply: No. Keep it. I have enough things that belong to me in other people's houses.

options.label: Take the sewing case and ask what is inside.
options.reply: The things she kept from the light. A button, a blue thread, and the name she used before yours.

options.label: Ask where they found it.
options.reply: In a room that had not chosen to be locked. Your mother left doors between.

options.label: Leave the case on the step.
options.reply: Good. Keep the seam where it is. Some houses only stay shut while nobody claims the key.

options.label: Say the dish is here and settle the debt.
options.reply: Then I'll call once, and no more. My mother would have called that decent.

options.label: Ask where the dish was last left before you look.
options.reply: On the dresser by the back door. Blue rim, hairline crack. I know a thing by its damage.

options.label: Say the previous tenant is not recorded here.
options.reply: No. That's not the same as saying she didn't owe me.
